source: Section numbers/titles from the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 22 of 2023) as published in the Gazette of India. Penalties crosschecked 2026-09-01 against the Schedule to the Act. See README.md. Subordinate rules are deliberately out of scope.
defaultPenalty: Up to ₹50 crore (residuary — Schedule to the DPDP Act, 2023)

provisions.title: Grounds for processing: personal data may be processed only for a lawful purpose for which the Data Principal has given consent (s.6) or for a legitimate use (s.7)
Notice to the Data Principal before or at the time of collecting personal data
Notice must itemise what personal data is collected and the specified purpose of processing
Notice must be available in English or a language listed in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution
Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by clear affirmative action
A request for consent must be accompanied by, or preceded by, the s.5 notice
A Data Principal may withdraw consent at any time, as easily as it was given; processing must cease within a reasonable time on withdrawal
Certain legitimate uses do not require separate consent (e.g. voluntarily provided data, employment, specified state functions, compliance with law)
General obligations of a Data Fiduciary: accuracy, processor contracts, and accountability for all processing done on its behalf
The Data Fiduciary is responsible for compliance with the Act for all processing undertaken by it or by a Data Processor on its behalf
A Data Fiduciary may engage a Data Processor to process personal data only under a valid contract
Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure effective observance of the Act
Reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach
Notify the Data Protection Board and every affected Data Principal in the event of a personal data breach
Erase personal data on withdrawal of consent or once the specified purpose is no longer served, unless retention is required by law
Publish the business contact information of a Data Protection Officer or other person able to answer Data Principal questions about processing
Establish an effective mechanism to redress the grievances of Data Principals
Processing a child's personal data requires verifiable parental consent; no tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising directed at children
Additional obligations of a Significant Data Fiduciary (India-based Data Protection Officer, independent data auditor, periodic Data Protection Impact Assessment and audit)
Right to obtain a summary of personal data processed and the processing activities carried out, and the identities of other Fiduciaries and Processors with whom it has been shared
Right to correction, completion, updating and erasure of personal data
Right of grievance redressal against a Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager, to be exercised before approaching the Board
Right to nominate another individual to exercise rights in the event of death or incapacity
Duties of the Data Principal (no false particulars, no impersonation, no frivolous complaints)
The Central Government may, by notification, restrict the transfer of personal data to specified countries or territories; stricter sectoral localisation requirements under other law are preserved
Central Government may restrict transfer of personal data to certain countries; specified exemptions apply
Exemptions from specified provisions (certain state processing, enforcement of legal rights or claims, research/archiving/statistical purposes, notified classes of Fiduciary)
